question: The web search subagent in your research system first had one tool, search_web, whose full description is "Searches the web." With that single tool, selection was reliable. The team then added search_papers, described only as "Searches for papers." Since then, news queries sometimes go to search_papers and paper queries sometimes go to search_web, although the search_web code and description are unchanged and the system prompt names neither tool. What best explains why tool selection became unreliable?

options.text: Adding search_papers introduced an error into the search_web code, so search_web fails on news queries and the model then retries them with search_papers.
options.reason: The stem says the search_web code is unchanged, and requests go to the wrong tool in both directions. That is a selection failure, which comes from the minimal descriptions the model relies on to choose.

options.text: The model selects tools mainly from their descriptions, and the two minimal descriptions give it no basis to separate two similar search tools.
options.reason: Tool descriptions are the main way the model selects tools. A minimal description was enough while there was no similar tool. Now two similar tools have minimal descriptions, so the model cannot reliably tell them apart.

options.text: The max_tokens limit of the subagent is too low for the model to compare two tools, so it now picks one of them without weighing the other.
options.reason: max_tokens only limits the length of the response. The model tells similar tools apart through their descriptions, and these two minimal descriptions give it nothing to compare.

options.text: The model favors the most recently added tool whenever two tools could apply, so search_papers now takes requests that belong to search_web.
options.reason: The guide gives no such recency rule; the model selects from descriptions. The misrouting also goes both ways, with paper queries going to search_web, which a preference for the new tool cannot explain.
